title_en: Chongqing Zhengtong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. v. Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce and Sichuan Huashu Animal Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. — trademark administrative dispute
ruling_gist_en: The 'agent' as stipulated in Article 15 of the Trademark Law includes not only trademark agents and representatives who, upon entrustment by the trademark registration applicant or registrant, handle trademark registration and other matters within the scope of authorization, but also agents and representatives in the sense of special sales agency relationships such as general distributors (exclusive distributors) and general agents (exclusive agents).

full_text_en:
Chongqing Zhengtong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce v. Sichuan Huashu Animal Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. — Administrative Dispute over Trademark

[2023] Ruling Summary

The term "agent" as used in Article 15 of the Trademark Law includes not only trademark agents or representatives who, upon authorization by a trademark registration applicant or trademark registrant, handle trademark registration and other matters within the scope of authority, but also agents or representatives in the context of special sales agency relationships such as exclusive distributorship (exclusive distribution) and exclusive agency (exclusive agency).

Administrative Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2007) Xing Ti Zi No. 2

Re-applicant (Third Party at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Chongqing Zhengtong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., Address: No. 77 Baocheng Road, Rongchang County, Chongqing.

Legal Representative: Hu Huailiang, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Hongyi, Attorney, Beijing Jinxin Lifang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yong, Attorney, Beijing Jinxin Lifang Law Firm.

Re-applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, Address: No. 8 Sanlihe East Road, Xicheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Hou Lin, Director.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ze, Officer, Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce.

Re-applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Sichuan Huashu Animal Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., Address: Group 4, Daqiao Village, Shengdeng Town, Longchang County, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Xiao Tizhong, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Kefei, Attorney, Beijing Dangdai Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Guobin, Attorney, Sichuan Taiwei Law Firm.

Re-applicants Chongqing Zhengtong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhengtong Company) and the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Review Board), in the case of an administrative dispute over trademark with Sichuan Huashu Animal Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huashu Company), dissatisfied with the Administrative Judgment (2006) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 93 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court on April 3, 2006, filed an application for retrial with this Court. Upon review, this Court decided to take up the case for retrial on March 19, 2007, by Administrative Ruling (2006) Xing Jian Zi No. 104-1. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Kong Xiangjun, Deputy Chief Judge of the Third Civil Division, serving as Presiding Judge, Judge Yu Xiaobai, and Acting Judge Xia Junli, and held a public hearing on May 24, 2007, with Clerk Bao Shuo serving as court recorder. Agent ad litem for the Re-applicant Zhengtong Company, Jiang Hongyi and Wang Yong, Agent ad litem for the Re-applicant Trademark Review Board, Wang Ze, and Agents ad litem for the Re-applicant Huashu Company, Zhu Kefei and Li Guobin, attended the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court and the Beijing High People's Court found the following facts through trial:

On September 12, 2002, Huashu Company filed an application with the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Office) for registration of the disputed trademark "头包西灵 Toubaoxilin". The trademark was approved for registration on February 7, 2004, with the trademark owner being Huashu Company, and the registration number being 3304260. The designated goods were veterinary preparations, veterinary drugs, veterinary biological preparations, etc., in Class 5. The term of exclusive use was from February 7, 2004, to February 6, 2014. On March 31, 2004, Zhengtong Company (then Chongqing Zhengtong Animal Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.) filed an application with the Trademark Review Board to revoke the disputed trademark, on the grounds that its registration violated Articles 10, 11(1)(a), 15, and 31 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Law). On March 4, 2005, the Trademark Review Board, in response to the trademark dispute raised by Zhengtong Company, rendered Ruling No. 289 [2005] in accordance with Articles 15, 41(2), and 43 of the Trademark Law, revoking the disputed trademark registered by Huashu Company in respect of goods such as veterinary drugs under Class 5.

On April 30, 2002, Zhengtong Company filed an application with the Chongqing Agricultural Bureau for the veterinary drug product "Compound Penicillin Potassium for Injection (Type I)", with the commodity name shown in the application form as "Cefalexin Powder for Injection", the manufacturer being Zhengtong Company, and the production permit number being Yu Shou Yao Sheng Zheng Zi No. 041. In the label sample attached to the application, the commodity name "Cefalexin" was presented in a special font and size and placed in a prominent position on the label.

On May 28, 2002, the Chongqing Agricultural Bureau, by Approval Certificate No. (2002) 533 under the authority of Chongqing Veterinary Drug Approval, approved Zhengtong Company to produce and sell the veterinary drug product with the generic name "Compound Penicillin Potassium for Injection (Type I)" and the commodity name "Cefalexin Powder for Injection", with the veterinary drug product approval number being Yu Shou Yao Zi (2002) X041008, the approval number valid until May 28, 2005.

On July 27, 2002, Zhengtong Company, as Party A, and Huashu Company, as Party B, entered into the "Agreement on Exclusive Sales of 'Cefalexin' Products" (hereinafter referred to as the Exclusive Sales Agreement). The main contents of the agreement are as follows: 1. Zhengtong Company authorized Huashu Company to exclusively sell the "Cefalexin" powder for injection products nationwide. Zhengtong Company shall not sell the product, and Huashu Company shall not produce the product, otherwise it would be considered a breach of contract. 2. The packaging would be designed by Huashu Company and printed by Zhengtong Company. The packaging would bear Huashu Company's "Huashu" trademark, and would be printed in the form of "developed by Huashu Company in cooperation, manufactured by Zhengtong Company", and the products would be organized for production by Zhengtong Company. 3. Huashu Company was responsible for marketing planning, product pricing, and bearing all costs such as sales expenses, advertising expenses, and transportation expenses for the exclusive sales area. 4. Huashu Company prepaid Zhengtong Company packaging costs of RMB 30,000. 5. Zhengtong Company provided product specifications and prices: 3g/vial × 120 vials/case, price RMB 108/case; if Huashu Company's cumulative sales reached 3,000 to 5,000 cases, the price would be RMB 106.80... 7. For any quality issues, Zhengtong Company would be responsible for returns and losses, and Huashu Company would be responsible for the outer packaging description. 8. Huashu Company must give advance notice for orders, and payment must be made in full before picking up goods from Zhengtong Company... 10. Upon expiration or early termination of the agreement, Zhengtong Company would continue to produce and sell the product, canceling Huashu Company's exclusive sales rights, but would not be allowed to continue using the "Huashu" trademark. 11. Taxes and debts incurred by Zhengtong Company during production and by Huashu Company during exclusive sales would be resolved separately by each party... 13. If "Cefalexin" were to be registered or other intellectual property issues arose, Huashu Company would be responsible, and Zhengtong Company would be responsible for re-applying to change the commodity name. After the agreement was signed, except for a change in the price stipulated in Article 5, which was actually performed, both parties performed the agreement as agreed.

During the period of cooperation, on the packaging of the products produced, the four characters "头孢西林" (Cefalexin) were used in a special font in a prominent position, with a font size significantly larger than the other text. The product packaging indicated: "Developed by Sichuan Longchang Huashu Animal Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., Manufactured by Chongqing Zhengtong Animal Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd." The registered trademark "Huashu" was used on the product packaging. The first sentence of the product description read: "This product is a dedicated effort from Huashu Company in 2002..." The outer packaging of the veterinary drug also contained promotional phrases such as "Huashu's dedicated offering, the veterinarian's first choice" and "You can confidently choose Huashu veterinary drugs".

On January 7, 2004, Zhengtong Company, as Party A, and Huashu Company, as Party B, entered into a "Termination Agreement" regarding the termination of cooperation on three varieties and nine specifications of products, including "Cefalexin", which stipulated that from January 7, 2004, Zhengtong Company would no longer produce the above varieties bearing the original pattern with the "Huashu" logo, and Huashu Company would not produce or process the above products bearing the production and approval markings of Zhengtong Company.

After the termination of the cooperative relationship, Zhengtong Company continued to produce Cefalexin powder for injection products. On the product packaging, "Cefalexin" was still used in a prominent position with a special font and size, and the registered trademark used on the product was "Anyi".

The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held: The issues in this case were whether the disputed trademark was Zhengtong Company's unregistered trademark, whether an agency relationship existed between Huashu Company and Zhengtong Company, and whether Huashu Company had registered Zhengtong Company's trademark without authorization.

"Cefalexin," as a commodity name, was independently applied for by Zhengtong Company to the relevant state authority on April 20, 2002, and was approved on May 28, 2002. It should be determined that "Cefalexin" was a commodity name first obtained by Zhengtong Company alone. In the process of applying for this commodity name, Zhengtong Company placed "Cefalexin" in a prominent position on the label sample and used a special font and size. After the commodity name was approved, during the cooperation between Zhengtong Company and Huashu Company, and after the termination of their cooperative relationship, the characters "Cefalexin" were consistently prominently used on the actual product packaging, with a clear difference in font, style, and size from other text on the packaging, giving it a strong distinctiveness. As a commodity name determined by Zhengtong Company itself, given that "Cefalexin" was consistently used in a prominent font and size in a prominent position on product labels or packaging, it objectively played the guiding role of indicating the source of goods, a function of a trademark. Moreover, since this commodity name was first obtained by Zhengtong Company, "Cefalexin" should be regarded as an unregistered trademark actually used by Zhengtong Company. The prominent part of the disputed trademark "头包西灵 Toubaoxilin" is the text "头包西灵", which is similar in character composition and pronunciation to Zhengtong Company's commodity name "头孢西林" (Cefalexin), and both are meaningless words. Since Huashu Company did not dispute the similarity between the disputed trademark and "Cefalexin," the Trademark Review Board's determination that the two groups of characters constituted similarity was upheld.

According to the Exclusive Sales Agreement signed between Huashu Company and Zhengtong Company, and the subsequent Termination Agreement to end the cooperative relationship, Zhengtong Company was the producer of the "Cefalexin" product, organizing production, providing product specifications and prices, and responsible for returns and losses in case of quality issues. Huashu Company, through Zhengtong Company's authorization, exclusively sold the "Cefalexin" powder for injection products nationwide, responsible for marketing planning in the exclusive sales area, product pricing, and bearing sales expenses, advertising expenses, and transportation costs. After signing the Termination Agreement, Huashu Company was not allowed to produce or process "Cefalexin" products bearing the "Chongqing Zhengtong Company production and batch markings." A sales agency legal relationship was formed between Zhengtong Company and Huashu Company. In that legal relationship, Zhengtong Company, as the producer and principal, granted authorization, thereby placing Huashu Company, as the seller, in the position of an agent.

Regarding the legal meaning of "agency" in Article 15 of the Trademark Law, including the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the current Chinese law's understanding of the concept of agency is no longer confined to Article 63 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China. Sales agency, as a legal activity in which an agent takes possession of the producer's products and sells them to third parties in the agent's own name or in the producer's name, is an inevitable result of the development of a market economy. A broad interpretation of "agency" in Article 15 of the Trademark Law to include sales agency is consistent with commercial practice and aligns with the legislative intent of the Trademark Law to maintain an honest and trustworthy market order. Huashu Company's unauthorized registration of a disputed trademark similar to Zhengtong Company's unregistered trademark was an act that violated the principle of good faith and should be prohibited by law.

In accordance with Article 54(1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court rendered a judgment upholding the Trademark Review Board's Ruling No. 289 [2005] on the Dispute over Trademark No. 3304260 "头包西灵 Toubaoxilin." The case acceptance fee of RMB 1,000 was to be borne by Huashu Company.

Huashu Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Beijing High People's Court.

The Beijing High People's Court held: The issues in this case were whether the commodity name "Cefalexin" had acquired the function of a trademark through use, and whether a legal relationship of principal and agent had been formed between Zhengtong Company and Huashu Company during their cooperation.

The function of a commodity name differs from that of a generic name; it is associated with a specific product and targets a particular product. In the veterinary drug product application submitted by Zhengtong Company to the relevant state authority, "Cefalexin" was listed as the commodity name, and in the submitted "Product Label Sample," it was used in a special font and size in a prominent position. Therefore, the first-instance court correctly determined that in practice, a commodity name can serve the function of a trademark in indicating the source of goods, and that "Cefalexin" was a commodity name first obtained by Zhengtong Company alone. Given that "Cefalexin" was consistently used in a prominent font and size in a prominent position on product labels or packaging, it objectively played the guiding role of a trademark in indicating the source of goods. Hence, "Cefalexin" should be regarded as an unregistered trademark actually used.

According to the terms of the Exclusive Sales Agreement and the actual performance, on the outer packaging of the veterinary drugs sold, besides the prominently marked commodity name "Cefalexin," there were also prominently marked the "Huashu" trademark, "Developed by Huashu Company, Manufactured by Zhengtong Company," and promotional phrases such as "Huashu's dedicated offering, the veterinarian's first choice" and "A dedicated effort by Huashu Company." Furthermore, considering that the entire sales market was responsible for marketing planning by Huashu Company, which also determined the sales price of the veterinary drugs and bore the costs of sales and advertising, and that there was no evidence that Zhengtong Company had sold veterinary drugs under the commodity name "Cefalexin" before cooperating with Huashu Company after obtaining the production license for the veterinary drug, it should be determined that the function of the commodity name "Cefalexin" in objectively indicating the source of goods, a function of a trademark, resulted from Huashu Company's promotional efforts, sales, and other uses. Since the actual user of the commodity name was Huashu Company, "Cefalexin" should be regarded as Huashu Company's unregistered trademark. The first-instance court's determination that "Cefalexin" was a commodity name first obtained by Zhengtong Company and that, because it was consistently prominently used on packaging during the cooperation and after the termination, it should be regarded as Zhengtong Company's actually used unregistered trademark, was inconsistent with the facts and is corrected.

Although Zhengtong Company first obtained the commodity name "Cefalexin," it did not use it in external sales from the time of obtaining it until the time Huashu Company applied for the trademark. Therefore, the name obtained only at the time of applying for the veterinary drug production license did not constitute a distinctive name of a well-known product. Although the prominent part of the disputed trademark "头包西灵 Toubaoxilin" is the text "头包西灵", which is similar in character composition and pronunciation to Zhengtong Company's commodity name "头孢西林" (Cefalexin), and both are meaningless words, and the two groups of characters are similar, Huashu Company, by using the commodity name "Cefalexin" itself, turned it into a trademark. Its application for the trademark "头包西灵 Toubaoxilin" did not violate the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 15 of the Trademark Law provides: "Where an agent or representative, without authorization, registers the trademark of the principal or the represented party in its own name, and the principal or the represented party raises an objection, the trademark shall not be registered and its use shall be prohibited." The "agent" in this provision refers to a trademark agent, i.e., a person who, upon authorization by a trademark registration applicant or a trademark registrant, handles trademark registration applications, requests investigation and punishment of infringement cases, or handles other trademark matters within the scope of authority. The "representative" refers to a trademark representative, i.e., a person who handles trademark registration and other trademark matters on behalf of the enterprise. In this case, the relationship formed between Huashu Company and Zhengtong Company based on the Exclusive Sales Agreement was a production and sales cooperative relationship. The first-instance court's determination that a principal-agent relationship was formed between them was clearly erroneous. Huashu Company, through its own use of the commodity name "Cefalexin," turned it into a trademark. Its application for the trademark "头包西灵 Toubaoxilin" did not fall within the circumstances described in Article 15 of the Trademark Law. Therefore, the Trademark Review Board and the first-instance court erred in determining that Huashu Company's application for the trademark "头包西灵 Toubaoxilin" violated Article 15 of the Trademark Law, and this error should be corrected.

In accordance with Article 61(3) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Beijing High People's Court rendered the following judgment: 1. The Administrative Judgment (2005) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 437 of the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court was set aside; 2. The Trademark Review Board's Ruling No. 289 [2005] on the Dispute over Trademark No. 3304260 "头包西灵 Toubaoxilin" was set aside. The case acceptance fees for the first instance and second instance were to be borne by the Trademark Review Board.

Both Zhengtong Company and the Trademark Review Board, dissatisfied with the second-instance judgment, filed applications for retrial with this Court.

Zhengtong Company's application for retrial argued: 1. The second-instance judgment misinterpreted the term "agent" as used in Article 15 of the Trademark Law. Whether based on the legal source, legislative intent of Article 15 of the Trademark Law, or referring to domestic and international enforcement practices, the "agent" mentioned in this provision is not limited to agents in trademark registration agency relationships but also includes distributors who, based on business dealings, may become aware of the principal's trademark. The second-instance court's limitation to "trademark registration agents" was clearly erroneous. 2. Based on a correct understanding of "agent" in Article 15 of the Trademark Law, and in light of the evidence in this case, it should be determined that an agency relationship existed between Zhengtong Company and Huashu Company. The second-instance court's determination on this issue was erroneous. 3. "Cefalexin," as a proprietary commodity name first obtained by Zhengtong Company alone and prominently used by Zhengtong Company on the veterinary drug products it produced, had already constituted an unregistered trademark actually used by Zhengtong Company. The second-instance court's determination that "Cefalexin" was Huashu Company's unregistered trademark was inconsistent with the facts. It requested the setting aside of the second-instance judgment and the upholding of the first-instance judgment and the Trademark Review Board's ruling.

Trademark Review and Adjudication Board argued in its retrial application: 1. The second-instance judgment's understanding of "agent or representative" in Article 15 of the Trademark Law deviated from the legislative purpose and was inconsistent with international practice. Article 15 of the Trademark Law originates from the Paris Convention, and the "agent or representative" stipulated therein is not limited to trademark agents and trademark representatives, but should include agents and representatives in sales agency relationships and representative relationships, as well as sellers of goods bearing the trademark owner's mark. 2. There was an error in fact-finding. It incorrectly defined the act of "sale," confused the relationship between veterinary drug product names, well-known veterinary drug product distinctive names, and trademarks, and treated the performance of the "Exclusive Product Sales Agreement" as the basis for determining the attribution of trademark rights. 3. It not only failed to properly resolve the trademark registration dispute but also created a new conflict between the trademark and the product name. Requested that the second-instance judgment be set aside, and that the first-instance judgment and the ruling of the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board be upheld.

Huashu Company argued in its defense that the second-instance judgment was correct and requested the rejection of the retrial applicant's application. The reasons were: 1. There was no principal-agent relationship between Huashu Company and Zhengtong Company; the rights and obligations stipulated in the Exclusive Product Sales Agreement did not have any agency characteristics, and the product packaging actually used by both parties in performing the contract also proved that Huashu Company was not a distributor of Zhengtong Company, let alone an agent. 2. "Toubaoxilin" was not an unregistered trademark of Zhengtong Company, but an unregistered trademark of Huashu Company; Huashu Company's registration of the "Toubaoxilin Toubaoxilin" trademark was consistent with the purpose of the contract entered into by both parties and did not violate the principle of good faith. 3. The Trademark Review and Adjudication Board's understanding and application of Article 15 of the Trademark Law was incorrect.

This Court finds upon retrial that the facts found by the original trial court are substantially true.

This Court further finds that Chongqing Zhengtong Animal Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. changed its name to Chongqing Zhengtong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. on November 15, 2006.

During the retrial hearing, the respondent Huashu Company submitted to the court document No. Chuan Xu Shi Han [2004] 204 of the Sichuan Provincial Animal Husbandry and Food Bureau, titled "Notice of the Sichuan Provincial Animal Husbandry and Food Bureau on Issuing Product Approval Numbers to Sichuan Longchang Huashu Animal Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.," and Huashu Company's aluminum bottle caps, to prove that the drug formulation of "Toubaoxilin" was in the public domain and not developed by Zhengtong Company; the aluminum bottle caps were marked with the Huashu trademark, were designed by Huashu Company, and that the relationship between Huashu Company and Zhengtong Company was a sales cooperation relationship rather than an agency relationship. Upon examination at trial, the aluminum bottle caps submitted by Huashu Company were merely supplementary evidence supporting the facts found at first instance and were related to the performance of the exclusive sales agreement, having no impact on the finding of facts in this case. Whether the drug formulation of "Toubaoxilin" indicated in document No. Chuan Xu Shi Han [2004] 204 of the Sichuan Provincial Animal Husbandry and Food Bureau was in the public domain is irrelevant to the finding of facts in this case.

Opinion of the Court

This Court is of the opinion that the issues in dispute in this case are: the scope of "agent" as stipulated in Article 15 of the Trademark Law; whether an agency relationship existed between Zhengtong Company and Huashu Company; and the attribution of the product name "Toubaoxilin."

(1) Regarding the scope of "agent" as stipulated in Article 15 of the Trademark Law.

Article 15 of the Trademark Law provides: "Where an agent or a representative, without authorization, seeks to register in its own name the trademark of the principal or the represented party, and the principal or the represented party raises an objection, the trademark shall not be registered and its use shall be prohibited." Since the parties, as well as the first-instance and second-instance judgments, have different understandings and determinations of the meaning of "agent" in this case, to eliminate the divergence and correctly apply the law, its meaning can be determined by referring to the legislative process, legislative intent, and the provisions of relevant international treaties.

This provision was added by the Trademark Law as amended on October 27, 2001. The "Explanation on the Draft Amendment to the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China," made by Wang Zhongfu, then Director of the former State Administration for Industry and Commerce, entrusted by the State Council at the 19th Session of the Standing Committee of the Ninth National People's Congress on December 22, 2000, stated: "Article 6-7 of the Paris Convention requires the prohibition of the agent or representative of the trademark owner from registering the said trademark in his own name without the authorization of the owner, and prohibits its use. Accordingly, and considering the increasing number of malicious registrations of others' trademarks in China, the draft adds the provision: 'Where an agent or a representative, without authorization, seeks to register in its own name the trademark of the principal or the represented party, and the principal or the represented party raises an objection, the trademark shall not be registered and its use shall be prohibited.'" Therefore, Article 15 of the Trademark Law is intended both to fulfill the treaty obligations under Article 6-7 of the Paris Convention and to prohibit acts of malicious registration of others' trademarks by agents or representatives. Article 6-7(1) of the Paris Convention provides: "If the agent or representative of the person entitled to a trademark in one of the countries of the Union applies for the registration of such trademark in its own name in one or more of the countries of the Union, without the authorization of such person, the latter shall be entitled to oppose the registration applied for or to demand its cancellation." According to authoritative commentaries on this treaty, the common practices of member states, and the consistent attitude of China's relevant administrative enforcement, "agent" and "representative" in Article 6-7 of the Paris Convention should be interpreted broadly, including agents or representatives in the sense of special sales relationships such as exclusive distributor and exclusive agent. With reference to Article 9 of the Supreme People's Court's "Regulations on Several Issues Concerning the Adjudication of International Trade Administrative Cases," which provides that "where there are two or more reasonable interpretations of a specific provision of the law or administrative regulation applicable by a people's court in adjudicating an international trade administrative case, and one of the interpretations is consistent with the relevant provisions of an international treaty concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China, the interpretation consistent with the relevant provisions of the international treaty shall be adopted, except for clauses on which the People's Republic of China has made reservations," the meaning of "agent" stipulated in Article 6-7 of the Paris Convention can serve as an important reference for interpreting Article 15 of China's Trademark Law.

Based on the above legislative process, legislative intent, the provisions of the Paris Convention, and with reference to the spirit of the above judicial interpretation, in order to prevent sales agents or representatives who, by virtue of a special distribution relationship, become aware of or use another's trademark from registering such trademark in bad faith in violation of the principle of good faith, the term "agent" in Article 15 of the Trademark Law should be understood broadly. It is not limited to trademark agents or representatives who act on behalf of a trademark registration applicant or trademark registrant within the scope of their authority for matters such as trademark registration, but also includes agents or representatives in the sense of special sales agency relationships such as exclusive distributor (exclusive distribution) and exclusive agent (exclusive agency). The second-instance judgment's understanding that "agent" under Article 15 of the Trademark Law refers only to trademark agents is incorrect and should be corrected.

(2) Regarding whether an agency relationship existed between Zhengtong Company and Huashu Company.

The market transaction relationship between Zhengtong Company and Huashu Company was established by the "Exclusive Product Sales Agreement" entered into by both parties. Whether an agency relationship as stipulated in Article 15 of the Trademark Law exists between the parties should be determined not only based on the name of the agreement but also, more importantly, based on the legal nature of its content. This agreement concerns the production and sale of "Toubaoxilin" powder injection products, with the main focus on sales. Article 1 of the agreement stipulates: "Zhengtong Company authorizes Huashu Company to exclusively sell the 'Toubaoxilin' powder injection product nationwide; Zhengtong Company shall not sell this product, and Huashu Company shall not produce this product, otherwise it shall be deemed a breach of contract." This indicates that the relationship formed between the parties is a type of exclusive sales relationship equivalent to exclusive distribution, and Huashu Company thereby obtained the exclusive sales qualification. It can be determined that Huashu Company is a sales agent within the meaning of Article 15 of the Trademark Law. Zhengtong Company's claim that an agency relationship existed between it and Huashu Company should be upheld. Huashu Company's defense that its relationship with Zhengtong Company was a sales cooperation relationship rather than an agency relationship cannot be established.

(3) Regarding the attribution of the product name "Toubaoxilin."

The focus of the dispute between the parties and a major point of divergence between the first-instance and second-instance judgments is the legal attribution of the product name "Toubaoxilin." Determining the attribution of this product name hinges on identifying who first obtained the name and whether subsequent use altered its attribution. Where one party originally acquires a specific product name, any change in its ownership must be caused by specific legal facts. Absent subsequent legal facts that alter its attribution, the ownership status remains unchanged.

The product name "Toubaoxilin" in dispute in this case is a unique drug product name originally obtained by Zhengtong Company through administrative approval. For this originally obtained unique drug product name, absent subsequent legal facts that change the attribution of rights, its ownership remains unchanged. In this case, the "Exclusive Product Sales Agreement" signed by Zhengtong Company and Huashu Company only stipulated that Huashu Company could jointly use the product name "Toubaoxilin." Huashu Company's acts of using, publicizing, and promoting the product name were merely acts of performing the agreement. Although Huashu Company's use, promotion, and marketing activities objectively enhanced the identifying function of the product name "Toubaoxilin," or, as found by the second-instance judgment, "the function of the product name 'Toubaoxilin' as a trademark in indicating the source of the goods was the result of Huashu Company's prominent publicity, sales, and other use activities," Huashu Company also received contractual consideration for this. This use in accordance with the agreement can, in essence, be regarded as a special use by Zhengtong Company. The factual state arising from this does not automatically alter the ownership of the disputed product name. In other words, Huashu Company's actual use of the trademark in accordance with the agreement does not constitute a legal fact that changes its ownership. On the contrary, the Exclusive Product Sales Agreement clearly stipulates the attribution of the product name "Toubaoxilin" in an agreed manner. Furthermore, the provision in the Exclusive Product Sales Agreement that "upon expiry or early termination of the agreement, Zhengtong Company may continue to produce and sell the product, cancel Huashu Company's exclusive sales rights, but shall not continue to use the 'Huashu' trademark," and the provision in the "Termination Agreement" regarding the termination of cooperation on three product varieties and nine specifications including "Toubaoxilin," which stated that "Zhengtong Company shall not, from January 7, 2004, continue to produce the above varieties printed with the original pattern bearing the 'Huashu' logo, and Huashu Company shall not produce or process the above products bearing Zhengtong Company's production and approval mark designations," indicate that after the termination of the cooperative relationship, the approval document designations, including the product name "Toubaoxilin," still belong to Zhengtong Company. Therefore, the attribution of the disputed product name "Toubaoxilin" is not changed by Huashu Company's publicity, use, and other activities during the period of the cooperative relationship. After the termination of the cooperative relationship, it still belongs to Zhengtong Company. Accordingly, the findings of the second-instance judgment that "the function of the product name 'Toubaoxilin' as a trademark in indicating the source of the goods was the result of Huashu Company's prominent publicity, sales, and other use activities; since the actual user of the product name was Huashu Company, 'Toubaoxilin' should be regarded as Huashu Company's unregistered trademark," and that "Huashu Company, by using the product name 'Toubaoxilin' itself and developing it into a trademark, its application to register the 'Toubaoxilin Toubaoxilin' trademark does not fall under the circumstances stipulated in Article 15 of the Trademark Law," are incorrect and should be corrected.

In summary, Huashu Company, by virtue of the exclusive sales relationship, used the product name "Toubaoxilin," which constituted an unregistered trademark of Zhengtong Company. After the termination of the exclusive sales relationship, Huashu Company registered on its own a trademark "Toubaoxilin Toubaoxilin" that is similar to the said product name, violating the provisions of Article 15 of the Trademark Law. The Trademark Review and Adjudication Board's ruling to cancel the registered trademark, and the first-instance judgment upholding that cancellation ruling, were not improper. The second-instance judgment applied the law incorrectly and should be corrected. Pursuant to Article 61, Item (2) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 76, Paragraph 1 and Article 78 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the Administrative Judgment No. (2006) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 93 of the Beijing High People's Court;

2. Uphold the Administrative Judgment No. (2005) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 437 of the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court.

The first-instance case acceptance fee is RMB 1,000, the second-instance case acceptance fee is RMB 1,000, totaling RMB 2,000, to be borne by the respondent, Sichuan Huashu Animal Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
